conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee, one of your hospital doctors. I understand you've been feeling more tired and short of breath lately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s been about a week. I’ve been needing oxygen all the time now—used to be just sometimes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And your legs were swelling too, right? You increased your water pill for that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I bumped my Torsemide to 125mg. It helped a little, but I still feel puffy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And your INR came back very high—7.1. That’s why we’re keeping you in, to watch for bleeding risks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that’s scary. I haven’t changed my warfarin. I take it just like my nurse tells me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We know. It might be the new batch from a different pharmacy. We’re holding warfarin for now until your INR comes down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need a transfusion or something?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, you’re not actively bleeding. We did see a positive stool test, but you’ve only had one episode. We’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My PCA saw blood once in my stool. I haven’t seen it again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. We won’t do a rectal exam unless needed. Your labs show mild anemia, but stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve also been more short of breath, even moving to the commode.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your oxygen requirement went up. But your chest X-ray looks clear—no signs of heart failure or infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Could it be my lungs? I have that ILD from my autoimmune disease.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your inflammatory markers—ESR and CRP are normal. CK is down from before. No sign of a flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So what’s making it harder to breathe?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We heard some wheezing. You responded well to a breathing treatment. We think it’s reactive airway disease.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Like asthma? I’ve never had that before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It can develop, especially with other lung conditions. We’ll send you home with an albuterol inhaler to use as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. What about my back and muscle pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re on Tylenol at home, and it’s helping. We don’t see signs of polymyositis flare, so we’ll keep your current meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m still thirsty. My mouth is dry.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your mucous membranes are dry. We’ll make sure you’re drinking enough. We’re also checking your electrolytes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your INR is down to 5.8 today—trending in the right direction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good, right? When can I restart warfarin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll wait until it’s below 3. Your home nurse will check it again soon, and you’ll restart based on that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my breathing? I used the albuterol last night and it helped.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. That supports our plan. No wheezing this morning. Keep using it as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I follow up with my pulmonologist?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your PCP will coordinate that. We think this is manageable with the inhaler for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your INR is now 4.7, still high but improving. No signs of bleeding. We’ll keep monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Any update on the stool test?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Urine culture showed contamination, not infection. Stool hasn’t been rechecked, but no new bleeding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel a bit stronger today. Less fatigued.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Your oxygen saturation is 99% on 2 liters. We’re confident you can go home tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about my other meds? I’m on so many.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll go home with all your usual medications except warfarin for now. We’re keeping the albuterol.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—your INR is stable, and you’re doing well. We’re discharging you today with services at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ll use the inhaler if I wheeze and wait for the nurse to check my INR.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Call if you have chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or any bleeding. Otherwise, follow up as planned.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I feel much better than when I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Glad to hear it. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up if needed.
